newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria says Cameroon attacks in disputed Bakassi.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria says Cameroon attacks in disputed Bakassi.

text.p: The Nigerian army says that neighbouring Cameroon has launched attacks in the disputed Bakassi peninsula where there may be significant oil reserves, national television said on Friday.

Army spokesman Lieutenant Colonel Godwin Ugbo was quoted as saying Cameroonian forces had fired on settlements in Atabong East, part of Bakassi, in recent weeks despite Nigeria's commitment to a peaceful solution of the dispute.
"Nigerian fishermen living in the area have been arrested by Cameroonian soldiers," Ugbo said.
The two African nations have clashed sporadically on Bakassi with heavy loss of life on both sides since 1994.
Troops of both countries are entrenched in the impoverished islands whose inhabitants are mainly fishermen and speak Efik, the language of southeastern Nigeria.
Cameroon took its case to the World Court in 1994 but the court's ruling in March forbidding further fighting did not prevent clashes a month later.
